column1: # --- combat: shots, damage, dismemberment, death; characters, motion, props ---

column3: per character: u16[bone][6], the asset slot the bone is redrawn with after each successive hit
per character: u16[bone][6], damage for each successive hit on that bone. char_adv00's head runs 100/120/140/160
per character: s8[bone][0x10], a difficulty addend on top of g_pBoneDamage
evt 0x2D: u16[group][3], the variant per player configuration
evt 0x2D: 0x40-byte {f32 x_offset, char text[0x3A], u16 end_frame} subtitle lines
evt 0x2D: u16[variant][4] subtitle line ids, 0xFFFF-terminated
6 death motions for the 0x8000 arc: 985, 989, 987, 988, 989, 990. Their root carries z by +7.4/+8.2
4 death motions for the 0x0000 arc: 985, 986, 988, 990. Their root carries z by -8.7/-9.5/-9.3
hinge swing curves, 6-byte {s16 rx, ry, rz} frames. Curve 2 is the van doors: 179 deg by frame 12, settling to 137
hinge swing curves, u16 yaw-only frames, for the selectors the xyz table has no entry for
hit candidates, stride 0x3C, sorted by the distance keys at 0x0059ECD8
entries in g_ShotHitList this frame
per player, 0x68 bytes: world ray origin, direction, -pitch/-yaw and their sin/cos
set to 1 by the player update when the trigger is down and ammo remains; cleared by ProcessPlayerShots

u8[16], bone -> destroyed-zone bit index for obj+0x1318. char_adv00: bone 2 (head) -> 0, bones 3-5 (right arm) -> 1, bones 6-8 (left arm) -> 2, all others 0xFF -- the shift is masked with 0x1F so those land harmlessly on bit 31.
s8[5], difficulty -> starting g_damage_rank: -3, -1, 1, 4, 8. Not clamped on the way in; UpdateDamageRank clamps to [0,15] on its first pass.
Adaptive 0..15 rank. DamageRankModifier indexes g_pBoneDamageByRank[char][bone*0x10 + rank] with it and adds the signed byte to the table damage.
int[2], per player: the bone index this player's shot hit. DispatchHit copies it from (s8)obj+0x190+player before calling ResolveHit.
int[2], per player, written by ResolveHit: 0 = nothing, 1 = damaged and part swapped, 2 = damaged only, 3 = severed, 5 = no effect (the effect table's `2` sentinel). Result 5 scores nothing.
+player*0x98. Added to the 120-point headshot award and then incremented by 10, so consecutive headshots pay 120, 130, 140 ...; any non-head hit zeroes it.
+player*0x98. Hits that scored, for the end-of-stage accuracy grade evt 0x2B reads.
u16[16], bone -> hit-reaction group. Eight groups partitioning the body: 1 head, 2 torso, 3 right arm (bones 3-5), 4 left arm (6-8), 5 pelvis (9), 6 right leg (10-12), 7 left leg (13-15).
15 sound ids for ActorPlayHitVoice: five flesh impacts (BLOOD02/03/04/06, BONE01), then hurt/kill/head voices as (set A, set B) pairs, then two two-entry pools.
Per character type -> per body condition -> a row whose entries at +0x10 are indexed by the last-hit zone (obj+0x1319). Taken only when obj+0x136C & 0x100, which is [open].

Per character type -> per body condition (obj+0x130C) -> u32[8] motion ids indexed by g_bone_reaction_group. Only two distinct rows exist for the humanoids: the ordinary one is head 977, torso 982, r.arm 981, l.arm 979, pelvis 974, r.leg 961, l.leg 960.
f32, stride 0xC, one per ring set. The middle radius; see g_enemy_approach_rings.
f32, stride 0xC, one per ring set. The outer radius; see g_enemy_approach_rings.
Added to g_enemy_approach_steps when the actor starts between the middle and outer rings.
Added on top of g_enemy_approach_steps_mid when the actor starts outside the outer ring, so a distant enemy walks further before it can attack.

s32[2], one per player, stride 4 -- not bytes; DAT_009A2BA4 is element 1. An approaching enemy must claim one through TryClaimAttackSlot before it may attack, so only g_max_attackers enemies commit at a time. The holder's index is kept in obj+0x121, and SelectCameraLookAtTarget focuses the camera on whoever holds one. Class 0x31 state 27 bypasses the claim and writes the slot itself.
Set when a claimed attack has actually started; TryClaimAttackSlot short-circuits while it is set.
The camera block's current look-at point (block+0xD8). StepCameraLookAtDamped eases it toward g_camera_lookat_target rather than snapping.
The point the camera *wants* to look at, chosen by SelectCameraLookAtTarget: a single attacking enemy, the midpoint of two, or the cam/ path's own target when no enemies are registered.
The look-at CamEvalPath7 evaluates from the path's target channels, independent of its eye channels -- which is how a path holds the eye still and sweeps the aim.
How many enemies may hold an attack permit at once: 1 or 2.

Four {inner, mid, outer} f32 ring sets copied into g_enemy_approach_rings by the scene reset. 25/38/51 for most characters, 37/48/51 for set 2. No stage script uses evt 0x0E, so these are what every encounter runs on.
10.0f. RegisterForCameraTracking's sort key is the distance from the camera eye times this, as an int.

Four 64-byte curves indexed by the look-at angle error clamped to 0x1FFF and shifted right 7. The scene reset selects curve 1: rate 64 below about 18 degrees, ramping to 16 past 23. A larger value is a SLOWER turn.
Zeroed by SelectCameraLookAtTarget when no enemy is registered; CameraTrackEnemiesTick uses it to choose between the angle-error curve and a flat rate.
Index into g_camera_turn_rate_curves; the scene reset sets 1.
The rate TurnLookAtToward divides by, refreshed every frame.
{u32 distance key; void *actor} pairs, at most 14, radix-sorted nearest-first before the slots are assigned.
How many entries g_camera_candidates holds this frame.

Per character type -> per body condition -> 0x10-byte attack entries: {s16 strike motion; s16 lunge motion; f32 distance; s16 hit frame; s16 player damage motion; u16 cancel mask}. The cancel mask names zones (1 head, 2 right arm, 4 left arm) whose destruction makes the strike whiff; 8 is outside the 3-bit mask and so never cancels.

Per character type -> per body condition -> s32[80]: which attack to use, indexed (rand%10 + (destroyed_zones & 7) * 10). Ten choices per destroyed-zone combination, so a zombie that has lost its head or an arm reaches for a different attack.
+player*0x98. PlayerTakeDamage decrements it by one per strike; the continue screen restores 1 or 2.
+player. Set to 0x5A by PlayerTakeDamage and counted down; a strike is ignored while it is non-zero.
Accumulates rank adjustments -- PlayerTakeDamage subtracts 2 -- and UpdateDamageRank adds it in and clears it on its next pass.
+player*0x98. Set by PlayerTakeDamage so the player entity plays its damage motion, which is stored alongside at g_player_hit_motion.
+player*0x130. The motion the player entity plays when hit, taken from the attack entry's +0x0A.
The wave-field manager: {u32 active count; u32 slot mask; f32 plane_y; u32; void *sources[8]}. Created by class 0x16, filled by class 0x17.
{handler, object size} per wave-source kind, stride 8: 0 travelling (WaveSourceTravellingTick), 1 circular (WaveSourceCircularTick).
0.01f. A circular ripple's amplitude scales by max(0, 1 - r * this), so it dies at 100 units.

Two rows of eight 0x10-byte entries, A at 00564818 (sets 0, 1 and 3) and B at 00564898 (set 2), indexed by obj+0x131A in the same layout as g_class30_attacks: {s16 strike; s16 lunge; f32 distance; s16 hit frame; s16 player damage motion; u16 cancel mask}. Each row is two groups of four -- right hand, left hand, unused, both-arms-gone -- and g_class31_attack_picks hands sets 0, 1 and 3 the indices 0, 1 and 3 and set 2 the indices 4, 5 and 6. Row A entry 3 is all zero.
The projectile's two states: flight (ThrownWeaponFlyToTarget) and deflected (ThrownWeaponDeflected). Sits immediately before g_class30_states.

Which player may be targeted, computed by SelectAttackablePlayer from g_two_player_game: -1 nobody, 0 player 0 only, 1 player 1 only, 2 both. TryClaimAttackSlot offers a permit accordingly when g_max_attackers is 1, and class 0x31 state 22 uses it to force a target when the claim fails.
Set when two players are actually in play. TryClaimAttackSlot's g_max_attackers == 2 branch picks a permit at random when this is set and falls back to the nearer player otherwise.

One float per character type, copied to obj+0x124 by EnemyZombieInit and EnemyThrowerInit. Paired with obj+0x128, which the zombie sets to 3.5 and the thrower to 5.0 (type 0x16) or 4.0 (types 0x17-0x19).

group*9 + member -> the live BreakablePropUpdate object, or 0 once it is destroyed. Stride 9 because the largest breakable group has nine members. The topple test reads it to find the props a member supports.

Per item-set: how many more props of that set must be destroyed before its hidden item drops. PlaceBreakableGroup seeds it with rand()%n + 1, so which break releases the item is random. Groups 6 and 7 both use set 2, so the later placement overwrites the earlier one's countdown.
96 x {s16 x, s16 y, s16 z}, scaled by 0.001, the prop's collision hull. BreakablePropGroundContact transforms all 96 to find which corner a toppling prop lands on.
15 x {s16 x, s16 y, s16 z} in thousandths -- where each shatter fragment starts, relative to the prop.
15 x {s16 rx, s16 ry, s16 rz} in BAMS -- each shatter fragment's initial orientation.
Per class-0x41-type-4 object kind, stride 0xC: {s16 effect_id @+0, s16 effect_arg @+2, ..., s16 radius @+8}. PlaceKindedProp copies them into the prop's +0x324/+0x328/+0x124.
Per item kind, stride 0xC: the u16 asset slot the pickup is drawn with. g_item_score_table is the s16 two bytes further into the same record.
Per item kind, stride 0xC: the float height the pickup is released at above the prop that hid it.

Selects which members of a breakable group PlaceBreakableGroup turns into one-shot targets (+0x11C = 1, asset 0x1A0F) while g_GameMode == 2: set 0 takes members 2, 3, 4 and 6; set 1 takes 0, 1 and 5; set 2 takes 0 and 6; set 3 takes the same four as set 0. What the four sets *are* is [open] -- the mode names come from the g_GameMode row, not from anything read here.

The event block currently executing, written by EvtAdvanceBlockOrRoute and recorded byte-wise into g_route_history. NOT g_evt_block_counter (0x009A2BB0), which is a monotonic count of block transitions and is what prop lifetimes measure.

g_camera_blocks + 0x80: the eased eye position of camera block g_camera_index, a vec3 FUN_00402EF0 eases toward the pose the path evaluated. FUN_00403B00 reads it as the eye when it measures the angle to the look-at target at block+0x98 (g_camera_block_target), which is what proves the three words are a position.

Which scene is loaded, zero-based -- ColiLoadForScene indexes its file list with it, so scene 1 is stage 2. Class 0x41 and class 0x40 branch on it for the per-stage sound sets and for PropExpireByBlockLifetime's scene-1 sweep.

29 pointers, one per effect id, to the root node of that effect's part tree: {u32 asset slot; s16 bone index; u16 child count; u32 children[]}. Same shape as g_character_skeletons but with no bind offsets -- an effect's translations come per-frame from its motion. Bounded by g_effect_bone_counts at 0x004D5404: 0x74 / 4 = 29 entries, and every tree's node count matches its bone count.
s16 per effect id: how many bones its motion frames carry, which is what fixes the frame stride align4(n * 0x12 - 0xF) = n translations of 0xC plus n rotations of 6.
u8 per effect id: 0 plays one motion key per frame; 1 and 2 halve the rate and interpolate, 2 additionally slerping through matrices when an axis differs by more than 0x3000.
Pointer per scene index to that scene's Original Mode item table, read by PickOriginalModeItem: stride 8, entries at +0..+3 (item ids) and cumulative rand() weights at +4..+7.
One 0xC record per Original Mode item id: u16 model slot, u16 second model slot, f32 draw scale, u16 pickup id passed to FUN_00475E40.
One byte per Original Mode item id, incremented on pickup and capped at 99.

Raised by CameraTrackEnemiesTick and CameraTurnOntoPathTarget once the eased look-at has caught up with the desired one (|VecCosSquaredSigned| > 0.99999). EvtOpWaitTargetsClear47 gates on it, so op 0x47 means nothing without the ease.

Selects how CameraEaseBlockEyeToPathPose moves the camera block's eye onto the path pose: set = a sixteenth a frame, clear = snap. Raised only by EvtActionSetFlag15; cleared by the scene reset and by EvtOpGotoSceneState31.

Four s32[6] rows at 005647B8, stride 0x18, indexed by obj+0x130C -- the behaviour set, which EnemyThrowerInit takes from the spawn descriptor's byte +1: +0 and +4 the idle pair (state 8 picks between them at random, or +0 for character type 0x17), +8 and +0C the walk pair picked by obj+0x34 bit 27 (states 7 and 18), +10 the landing clip (states 10 and 25), +14 the airborne clip (state 2). Set 0 is zstin, set 1 zsass, set 2 zskamere, set 3 zslman.

Three rows of 0x10-byte entries at 00564E58 (set 0, five stances), 00564F98 (sets 1 and 2, one stance) and 00564FD8 (set 3, five stances), indexed attack + stance*4 where the stance is obj+0x136C bit6 + bit7*2 + bit8*3 -- the surface: ground, one wall, the other, ceiling -- plus 4 while bit 17 marks a pounce. The entry is {u32 pointer to a 12-dword arc motion script; s32 hit frame, -1 meaning the arc's landing phase; s32 player damage motion; u32 cancel mask}.

Two s32[8][10] blocks at 00565118 (sets 0, 1 and 3) and 00565258 (set 2), read as a byte at (rand()/16 % 10 + (obj+0x1318 & 7) * 10) * 4 and stored to obj+0x131A. Intact gives a coin flip between the right hand (0 or 4) and the left (1 or 5), one arm gone forces the other, and both arms gone gives the head-butt slot (3 or 6).
Four rows of three pointers, stride 0xC, one per behaviour set; the band index is 0 unused, 1 for 40 < distance <= 50 and 2 for everything else. Reached through g_class31_action_picks.

Per behaviour set, a pointer to a three-pointer band row in g_class31_action_pick_bands; each band points at an s32[8][10] of candidate state ids drawn as (rand()/16 % 10 + (obj+0x1318 & 7) * 10) by ThrowerPickNextState and gated by ThrowerTryEnterState. Band 0 is unreachable. Set 0 -- zstin -- is the only one that climbs: its band 1 is 14, 15, 16 and 12 and its band 2 is 7 and 13, where sets 1 and 3 only ever offer 7 and the throw, and set 2 offers nothing but 7.

Two s32[8] rows indexed by g_bone_reaction_group[obj+0x1368], and the split is by motion bank rather than by behaviour: row A at 00565D98 is szom.bin (bank 47), which sets 0, 1 and 3 share because character types 0x16, 0x18 and 0x19 are all sixteen-bone szom skeletons, and row B at 00565DB8 is kame.bin (bank 20), set 2's, because zskamere is a twenty-four-bone skeleton of its own. That is why every table in this class has exactly two distinct rows.

s32[8][2] pose frames for motions 0x3D9 to 0x3E0, addressed as the base plus ((rand()%17 >> 4) + motion*2 - 0x7B2) * 4 with no bounds check: 3D9 {104,98} 3DA {96,84} 3DB {76,75} 3DC {160,152} 3DD {83,80} 3DE {83,82} 3DF {94,91} 3E0 {73,70}. Class 0x31 never plays a motion in that range, so every use of this fallback reads outside the array -- ThrowerStateFallToSurface hands the corpse states 0x3A5, 0x3A9 or 0x1BA, which land in mesh floats at 005928E0 and 00592900 and in a string at 00591988. The four special-cased tables cover every other entry path.
Corpse pose frames {44, 35} for motion 0x3A6, the airborne clip of behaviour sets 0 and 3.
Corpse pose frames {18, 21} for motion 0x1BC, character type 0x17's death clip.
Corpse pose frames {48, 40} for motion 0x11D, the death clip of character types 0x18 and 0x19.
Corpse pose frames {74, 70} for motion 0x11E, character type 0x16's death clip.
One 0x30-byte three-stage arc motion script per enemy slot, indexed by obj+0x3C. InstallArcMotionScript copies into it and ActorArcStep walks it.
State 10's arc motion script for character type 0x16: {0x001,3,5,16}{0x001,17,5,24}{0x001,25,5,34}.
State 15's arc motion script {0x123,0,5,15}{0x123,16,5,33}{0x123,34,5,43}; on completion the state sets obj+0x136C bit 6.
State 14's arc motion script {0x122,0,5,15}{0x122,16,5,33}{0x122,34,5,43}; on completion the state sets obj+0x136C bit 7.
State 16's arc motion script {0x135,0,5,29}{0x135,30,5,59}{0x135,60,5,87}; on completion the state sets obj+0x136C bit 8.
State 10's arc motion script for character type 0x19 and any type other than 0x16, 0x17 and 0x18: {0x11A,0,5,38}{0x11A,39,0,65}{0x11A,66,0,79}.
State 10's arc motion script when obj+0x131A is 3 and the character is not 0x18: {0x11A,30,5,38}{0x11A,39,0,65}{0x11A,66,0,79}.
State 10's four arc motion scripts for character type 0x18, one per stance at stride 0x30: motions 0x1EB, 0x1F9, 0x1EF and 0x201, each cut {0,5,1}{2,5,21}{22,0,43}.
State 20's arc motion script for characters other than 0x17, chosen at random from this and the byte-identical copy at 00564948: {0x12C,50,0,55}{0x12C,56,0,63}{0x12C,64,5,98}.
Arc motion script {0x1B7,0,0,19}{0x1B7,20,0,31}{0x1B7,32,0,42}, used by character type 0x17 in states 20 and 26.
State 26's arc motion script when the waypoint's style word is 1: {0x12D,12,1,12} three times.
State 26's arc motion script when the waypoint's style word is 2: {0x12D,7,0,11}{0x12C,48,1,65}{0x12D,17,1,22}.
State 26's arc motion script for any other waypoint style: {0x12D,0,0,8}{0x12D,9,0,17}{0x12D,18,0,23}.

int[2]: which players resolve a hit this frame and in what order, written by ChooseHitPlayerOrder -- 0 or 1 in slot 0 for a one-player game, a randomised pair for two, -1 for an unused slot. This is the array ZombieOnShot and ThrowerOnShot walk; it is not g_hit_slots at 0x009C88C0.
s32[8], reaction group to stumble motion, shared by behaviour sets 0, 1 and 3: 3A7 3A3 3A7 3AA 3AB 3A7 3A2 3A1.
s32[8], the same for behaviour set 2 (zskamere): 1BD 1BD 1BD 1BF 1BE 1BD 1BD 1BD.

One of the three free-running counters FUN_0040E730 steps once a game tick, beside g_frame_counter (0x009A32A0) and DAT_009A2BAC. Class 0x31 states 5, 27 and 34 read its low bit for the blink parity, which is the only use found -- what distinguishes it from the other two is [open].

Camera block 2's current path frame -- the same +0xD0 field again, at g_camera_blocks + 2*0x1A4. A scripted state waiting on a camera cue accepts either this or g_cam_path_frame: class 0x31 state 27 does, and so does class 0x33 at 0x00433B1A.
